extracted.intended_audience: general readers, inventors, law students, and practitioners seeking an overview of Australian patent law
extracted.subtask_description: A high-level encyclopedic summary of the legal and procedural standards governing patents in Australia, including statutory framework, key patentability concepts, procedural features (e.g. first-to-file, patent terms), and historical/administrative notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents Act 1990 (primary legislation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary piece of legislation is the Patents Act 1990.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as the main statutory framework governing patents in Australia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration by IP Australia
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are administered by the Commonwealth Government agency IP Australia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IP Australia is the government body responsible for patent examination, granting and administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership of international agreements (WIPO, TRIPS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Australia is a member state of the World Intellectual Property Organization, and compliant with Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This international membership and compliance makes Australian patent law broadly comparable with patent law in other major countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard patent term
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard patent with a term of 20 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as the ordinary maximum term for a standard patent in Australia.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-to-file system
rubrics_metrics.description: Australia operates a first to file system, like much of the rest of the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority to the first applicant to file a patent application, rather than to the first to invent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation patent (historical/eligibility and features)
rubrics_metrics.description: An innovation patent offered a lower threshold for inventiveness, and a maximum term of 8 years; innovation patents had a faster approval process and lower fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovation patents were being phased out: the last date for filing an innovation patent in Australia was 25 August 2021.

rubrics_metrics.name: AusPat Patent database
rubrics_metrics.description: The AusPat Patent database is the official Australian patents database operated by the Australian Intellectual Property Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AusPat records patents dating back to 1904 and is the official public record for Australian patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable subject matter
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under 'Patentability requirements and related concepts' as a core concept determining what inventions may be protected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a legal concept related to patents; pertains to who qualifies as an inventor for purposes of rights and entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a fundamental patentability requirement: the invention must be new relative to the prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step and non-obviousness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a core patentability requirement indicating the invention must not be obvious to a person skilled in the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a requirement for patentability — the invention must be capable of some practical application in industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included among related patentability concepts; the invention must have some use or utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person skilled in the art
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A legal benchmark used in assessing inventive step/non-obviousness and other standards; listed among related concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The body of existing knowledge against which novelty and inventive step are assessed; listed among key concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as an 'other legal requirement' — the patent specification must adequately disclose the invention so that a person skilled in the art can carry it out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as an 'other legal requirement' — applications should relate to a single inventive concept or set of closely related inventions.
